newsitem.title: UK: Dollar steady before data, poised to push higher.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady before data, poised to push higher.

text.p: The dollar was supported at midsession on Tuesday after regaining ground lost overnight, but now needs a kickstart to set new highs, analysts said.
While profit-taking pulled the dollar off Monday's peak of 1.8490 marks, its highest since November 1989, positive data or gains in U.S. assets will help it rebound, traders said.

"It's been fairly quiet today with the dollar caught below psychological levels at around 1.84 marks," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets. "However, the dollar is well underpinned and it is only a matter of time before it starts moving higher and makes new highs against the mark."

A buy signal could come from the U.S. employment cost index at 1230 GMT, which economists expect to show a rise of 0.8 percent in the second quarter after climbing 0.6 in the first. Confirmation that inflation is under control would bolster U.S. assets and hence the dollar.
But some analysts said the market may have to wait for Friday's payroll data for a reliable catalyst.

"There's still a good chance the dollar can reach 1.85 which would be very bullish technically," said First Chicago economist Teis Knuthsen. "But the market is getting a bit more hesitant and is looking for confirmation of the uptrend."
The dollar stood at 1.8350/60 marks at 1105 GMT, down from 1.8470/80 late Monday in Europe.

It slipped slightly to 117.50/55 against the yen compared with 117.60/70 at the previous close in Europe. Still it proved resilient for most of the morning to U.S. criticisms of the automotive trade situation with Japan and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's comments that Japan should not run a significant trade surplus.
"When the dollar is up against the yen people worry about the trade implications because of Japan's increasing trade surplus," said Bank of Boston dealer Peter Wood.
"But it's only temporary weakness as fundamentals still suggest the dollar should firm against the yen," said Wood.
"There's a lot of resistance at 118 yen but over the course of time we could see an attempt at 120. The authorities won't want to see it any higher than that."
Former Japanese vice finance minister Makoto Utsumi said earlier a range of 110-120 yen to the dollar was not a problem but a yen weaker than 125 per dollar would be excessive.
Cable came off lows, firming to $1.6340/45 at 1140 GMT from $1.6321/26 on Monday as sterling found support after its 2.5 percent tumble against the mark.
"Cable is off its lows but it hasn't recovered much," said Juckes. "People are pretty skittish on sterling short term."
Talk that Britain may hold off another rate rise at the Bank of England's monetary policy meeting next week still weighs on the pound and could see more pressure on the downside, said analysts.
